evals.prompt: Help me design the architecture for my SaaS. It's for managing gym memberships.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not propose a stack yet. It notes there is no repo context, states what it already knows (a SaaS for gym memberships), and asks the phase 1 questions — purpose in one sentence, success criterion, non-goals, new vs. replacement — at most four, each with a default the user can accept.
expectations: Response asks questions from phase 1 (problem & goals) only, not from later phases
Response asks at most four questions
Response offers a default answer for each question so the user can reply 'yes'
Response does not propose a language, framework, database, or hosting platform yet
Response says it will continue one phase at a time

evals.prompt: Design the v1 architecture for this project. The repo has a Gemfile with rails 7.2 and pg, a Dockerfile, config/deploy.yml for Kamal deploying to a Hetzner VPS, and .github/workflows/ci.yml running rspec. README says it's an internal tool for our support team to manage refund requests. No docs/ folder yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill confirms in one or two lines what the repo already decides — Rails 7.2, PostgreSQL, Kamal on a Hetzner VPS, GitHub Actions CI — and does not ask about language, framework, database, or hosting. It starts the interview at phase 1 with the internal-tool context already applied (e.g. users are the support team) and asks only what is still open.
expectations: Response states that Rails, PostgreSQL, Kamal/Hetzner hosting, and GitHub Actions CI are already decided by the repo
Response does not ask which language, framework, database, or hosting to use
Response treats the support team as the known user type rather than asking who the users are from scratch
Response asks the remaining open questions one phase at a time with defaults

evals.prompt: Here's everything: a B2B scheduling tool for ~30 dental clinics in Uruguay, each clinic sees only its own data. Core flows: book appointment, send reminders by WhatsApp/SMS, patient records, monthly billing report. Money flow is booking. Team: 2 Rails devs, 3-month deadline, budget under 300 USD/month, no compliance beyond local privacy law. Availability: an hour down is annoying but not fatal. Latency under 1 s. Data: < 100k appointments/year. Integrations: Twilio for messaging. No public API. Host on Fly.io, staging + prod, devs are on call. Propose the architecture.
evals.expected_output: The gate is satisfied, so the skill moves to synthesis and presents a short proposal in chat: ranked drivers (2 devs / 3 months, per-clinic isolation, no double-booking), a modular monolith on Rails with PostgreSQL, a job queue for reminders, shared-database multi-tenancy with a clinic_id scope, Fly.io hosting. It lists alternatives considered (microservices, schema-per-tenant, hosted pub/sub) with why they lost, and asks for objections before writing the document.
expectations: Response does not ask further interview questions before proposing
Response lists ranked architectural drivers derived from the brief
Response recommends a modular monolith with a single PostgreSQL database and a job queue for reminders
Response recommends shared-database multi-tenancy with a clinic/tenant scope rather than a database per clinic
Response names at least one alternative it rejected for a major decision and gives the driver-based reason
Response asks for objections or confirmation before writing docs/architecture.md

evals.prompt: We're 2 engineers building an MVP marketplace in 4 months. I want to go with microservices from the start — one for users, one for listings, one for payments, one for notifications — on Kubernetes, so we're ready to scale. Go ahead and design it that way.
evals.expected_output: The skill states the trade-off once in a couple of sentences — four services and Kubernetes on a 2-person team in 4 months costs distributed transactions, four pipelines, and ops time, with no named driver — and recommends a modular monolith with those four modules, noting extraction later is a refactor. It asks whether the user still wants services; if the user reaffirms, it proceeds, records the decision as the user's with their reason, and puts the monolith alternative in the decision log.
expectations: Response states the trade-off of microservices and Kubernetes for a 2-person team with a 4-month deadline
Response recommends a modular monolith with users, listings, payments, and notifications as modules
Response pushes back only once and asks whether the user wants to keep their choice
Response says that if the user reaffirms, the design will follow their decision and the decision log will record it as a user decision with the alternative noted
Response does not refuse or silently ignore the user's stated preference

evals.prompt: The proposal looks good, go ahead and write the document.
evals.expected_output: The skill prints the complete architecture document in chat (all sections: header, overview, non-goals, drivers, quality attributes, mermaid diagram, modules, data model, key flows, integrations, infrastructure, cross-cutting, decision log with alternatives, risks & open questions, evolution path), then runs `mkdir -p docs` and saves the identical markdown to docs/architecture.md, leaving it unstaged. It does not scaffold code, create other files, or commit.
expectations: Response prints the full document in chat rather than a summary that points to the file
Response saves the document to docs/architecture.md and creates the docs directory if it does not exist
Response includes a decision log where every row has alternatives and a driver-based rationale
Response includes a risks & open questions section listing assumptions taken from defaults
Response does not create any file other than docs/architecture.md and does not git add, commit, or push

evals.prompt: We already have docs/architecture.md from three months ago (Rails modular monolith, Postgres, Sidekiq, Fly.io, single-tenant). We just signed a deal that requires supporting multiple companies with isolated data, and the customer needs SSO. Update the architecture.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the existing document, treats its decision log as settled, and runs only the interview phases the change touches (users & tenancy, constraints/compliance, auth). It then proposes shared-database multi-tenancy with a tenant scope and an SSO provider, and delivers an updated docs/architecture.md that keeps existing decision-log rows (marking the single-tenant one superseded) and adds a 'Changes since last version' section.
expectations: Response reads the existing docs/architecture.md before asking anything
Response asks only about what changed (tenancy, SSO, compliance) and does not restart the full seven-phase interview
Response keeps unchanged decisions such as Rails, Postgres, Sidekiq, and Fly.io as they are
Response marks the previous single-tenant decision as superseded rather than deleting it
Response adds a 'Changes since last version' section to the updated document
Response overwrites docs/architecture.md and leaves it unstaged
